parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Section four. You will hear part of a lecture about factors you should consider when creating advertising materials and the effects they can have on your product sales. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Hello, class, and welcome back to Marketing Strategies. This week, I will expand upon last week's lecture by talking about factors you should consider when creating advertising materials and the effects they can have on your product sales. Lesson one: limit your advertising to the geographic area of your target market.

Though you may have a product that people want in a large area, the distance that customers are willing to travel is a significant factor in their choice of where to purchase that product. Take this example. If you're really hungry and decide you want a burrito, would you choose the restaurant that is a block from your apartment or the one that is just as good, or even slightly better, across town? Of course, you'd pick the closer restaurant.

Next, there's the method of communication to your target market. How do you decide among radio ads, TV commercials, flyers, or even word of mouth? While we often think of the visual presentation of ads, there's much more to advertising than the look. Studies show that consumers are much more likely to remember advertising slogans if there's also a sound played. Did you know that your sense of smell is closely linked with memory? Think about Mandy's Candy Store up the road. Every time you walk past it, you can just smell the chocolate, right? I bet you can almost smell it now. Just mentioning the name brings about the smell memory and, in turn, a chocolate craving. What better way to sell chocolate bars?

Obviously, sometimes appealing to the senses isn't the most practical way to advertise. For example, it's a good idea to come up with a marketing strategy that adapts to the product, especially digital products. The flexibility of this kind of products is extremely important, so it's very common for advertisers to form one single layout for all of their ads, the visual, the medium, even the majority of the content, and simply update the ad each time they come out with a new version. Remember, advertising is all about stirring up the right feeling in your potential customers, whether by stimulating the senses, appealing to the intellect, and so on. Once the customer experiences the ad, the important thing is his or her reaction. Someone could love the ad you made, but unless he or she considers buying the product, you failed to get the reaction you were looking for.

So once you have successfully reached your target customer and you have his or her business, often you'll want to expand to a larger market. More often than not, the same marketing strategies you used in your small campaign may not work for a larger audience. The larger you scale your product, the more factors you must consider.

For instance, Apple operates worldwide, so they must tailor their advertising for each market they enter. Often you'll see Apple ads on international flights that appear not only in English, which is the lingua franca of most regions, but also in the native languages of the majority of passengers.

I traveled to Russia last week, and it was really interesting to see the same Nike ad that I've seen a hundred times, except this time it was in Russian.

Okay, going back to the medium of the advertisement, even after choosing to create print ads instead of radio announcements, television commercials, et cetera, there is more to consider. If you print your ad in a newspaper, it will be read by a far different audience than if you print your ad in a popular magazine. Would you put an ad for the new Justin Bieber album in a newspaper? Probably not, because that product is most suitable for youths.

Let's face it, do you know anyone under the age of twenty-five that buys a newspaper? No. Now let's try a few strategy exercises.

Imagine you are a company that is aiming to improve the environment by making products that reduce human waste. How would you advertise your product? Clearly, it would send the wrong message if you put up flyers or other materials that caused lots of waste paper.

Consider instead putting commercials on the health channel or buying ad space on websites like UNESCO.

Or here's another example. What is one great place to advertise suntan lotion? How about a swimming pool? It has the exact group of people that need the product. All right, one last thing. Let's say you're filming a commercial for a water filter pitcher. What would be good scenery to use for the background? Think about somewhere calm and relaxing with clean, fresh water. Can't you see how much more effective a commercial with the beautiful scenery and flowing rivers of a national park would be than, say, water dripping from a tap? So to wrap things up today, think about the geography of your target market, the type of marketing material you should use, and the most effective way to appeal to the customer in order to make a successful ad campaign. That is all I have for you today. Make sure to read through chapter eight for Monday if you have not done so already.

Okay, now I'd be happy to answer any questions you may have.

That is the end of Section four. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到顾客愿意出行的“distance（距离）”是他们选择去哪里购买产品的重要因素，这直接对应了题干中的“affects the probability”。
你可能在后面听到了关于餐厅远近的例子，但填空考查的是概括性的核心词，不要被具体的场景例子（如restaurant、apartment）带跑偏。
Though you may have a product that people want in a large area, the distance that customers are willing to travel is a significant factor in their choice of where to purchase that product.
录音指出，如果广告标语播放时伴随着“sound（声音）”，消费者会更容易记住，完美契合题干的“easier to remember”和“played with”。
你可能会在前面听到visual presentation（视觉呈现）就急着找词填，但要注意题目中有明确的条件关联词“if”，所以要等听到“if”引导的句子再下笔。
Studies show that consumers are much more likely to remember advertising slogans if there's also a sound played.
录音用Mandy's Candy Store作为例子，说明了嗅觉（sense of smell）能唤起记忆并引发对巧克力的渴望，从而吸引顾客。
你可能会在听到“memory”或“chocolate”时急于下笔，但题干问的是“sense of _____”（什么的感官），必须要填入具体的感官smell。

Did you know that your sense of smell is closely linked with memory? Think about Mandy's Candy Store up the road. Every time you walk past it, you can just smell the chocolate, right? I bet you can almost smell it now. Just mentioning the name brings about the smell memory and, in turn, a chocolate craving.
录音直接点明，对于数字产品（digital products）这类商品来说，其“flexibility（灵活性）”是极其重要的（extremely important）。
你可能会被后面罗列的一长串名词（如layout, visual, medium）干扰，但只有flexibility紧跟了“extremely important”这个核心限定词，所以抓住修饰语就能排除干扰。

For example, it's a good idea to come up with a marketing strategy that adapts to the product, especially digital products. The flexibility of this kind of products is extremely important, so it's very common for advertisers to form one single layout for all of their ads, the visual, the medium, even the majority of the content, and simply update the ad each time they come out with a new version.
录音中清晰地表述，一旦顾客体验了广告，真正重要的就是他或她的“reaction（反应）”。
你可能会在听到buying the product时犹豫，但题干的主语是顾客体验广告后的“某件事/态度”，填入reaction最符合语境且直接对应录音。

Once the customer experiences the ad, the important thing is his or her reaction. Someone could love the ad you made, but unless he or she considers buying the product, you failed to get the reaction you were looking for.
录音提到在国际航班上，广告除了使用英语，还会使用大多数乘客自己的母语“languages（语言）”。
你可能一听到English就觉得答案出来了，但English前面有“not only”作为并列排除，题目要找的是属于“多数乘客（most passengers）”的东西，对应的是native languages。
Often you'll see Apple ads on international flights that appear not only in English, which is the lingua franca of most regions, but also in the native languages of the majority of passengers.
录音中主讲人反问“你认识25岁以下买 newspaper（报纸）的人吗？没有”，这直接等于题干所说的“很少有年轻人买报纸”。
你可能会听到前面的专辑（album）就填了，但那是录音里说适合年轻人买的东西，题目问的是年轻人“很少买（very few... buy）”的东西，必须听懂录音里的反问语气。
Probably not, because that product is most suitable for youths. Let's face it, do you know anyone under the age of twenty-five that buys a newspaper? No.
录音开头就设定了一个旨在改善“environment（环境）”的公司场景，随后给出的建议之一就是在像UNESCO这样的网站上打广告。
你可能会因为UNESCO出现在一整段话题的末尾而跟丢，这道题的答案其实在“话题刚引入”的时候就已经提前给出了，要习惯带着题干的前后信息一起听整体语义。

Imagine you are a company that is aiming to improve the environment by making products that reduce human waste. How would you advertise your product? Clearly, it would send the wrong message if you put up flyers or other materials that caused lots of waste paper. Consider instead putting commercials on the health channel or buying ad space on websites like UNESCO.
录音提问防晒霜去哪做广告好，马上回答说“swimming pool（游泳池）”是个好地方，因为那里有刚好需要该产品的人群。
你可能对suntan lotion就是sunscreen（防晒霜）的同义替换不敏感导致愣神，从而错过了紧跟在问题后面的答案，遇到生词一定要迅速往后听地名/场所。
What is one great place to advertise suntan lotion? How about a swimming pool? It has the exact group of people that need the product.
录音在探讨净水器广告背景时指出，展现“national park（国家公园）”里的美丽风景和河流，会是非常有效的广告场景。
你可能会听到后面有tap（水龙头）这个地点词，但录音明确说了国家公园比水龙头滴水更有效（more effective... than...），tap只是被比下去的错误示范。

Let's say you're filming a commercial for a water filter pitcher. What would be good scenery to use for the background? Think about somewhere calm and relaxing with clean, fresh water. Can't you see how much more effective a commercial with the beautiful scenery and flowing rivers of a national park would be than, say, water dripping from a tap?
